title: Erdos #1159: Bounded Blocking Sets in Projective Planes

problemStatement.formal: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every finite projective plane has a blocking set meeting each line in at least one point and at most C points?
problemStatement.plain: Can every finite projective plane be blocked by a point set whose intersection with every line is uniformly bounded, independent of the plane order?
whyMatters: Turns the known logarithmic blocking-set bound into a uniformity question about finite projective planes.
Separates small blocking sets from blocking sets with bounded line intersections.
The Lean file highlights the gap between per-order O(log n) bounds and a single absolute constant.

proven: Lean defines IsBlockingSet for generic incidence structures and proves monotonicity plus non-triviality of the empty set.
Mathlib-backed projective-plane facts are exposed for point counts, line counts, and total points/lines.
The theorem ess_implies_per_order_bound derives per-order bounds from the axiomatized Erdos-Silverman-Stein logarithmic result.
open: The absolute constant blocking-set conjecture remains open.
The Erdos-Silverman-Stein O(log n) theorem is an active axiom, not proved from Mathlib.
The Lean conjecture uses a natural-number constant C and does not encode a separate C > 1 side condition.
knownResults.goal: Keep the known logarithmic bound, the projective-plane infrastructure, and the open uniform-constant conjecture clearly separated.

currentState.focus: Metadata now describes the blocking-set scaffold, Mathlib projective-plane anchors, and the single ESS axiom without claiming the uniform constant conjecture is solved.
currentState.nextAction: A useful proof slice would formalize more concrete finite-plane examples or sharpen the bridge from logarithmic per-order bounds to uniform-bounded variants.
